body.statement:
There is a constant \(C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\), there is a total computable estimator \(T\in\mathcal T_{n,m,d}\) satisfying
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}
E[(T-\tau(P))^2]
\le C_\epsilon\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\left(\frac{d}{n+m}\right)^2\right\}.
\]
Consequently the same expression upper-bounds \(R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\).
body.proof_tex:
For \(n\ge12\), reserve the first \(\lfloor n/3\rfloor\) labeled observations as an outcome pool and concatenate the remaining labeled \((X,A)\)'s with all auxiliary observations as a marginal pool.  These pools are independent by \(\texttt{ass:labeled-iid}\), \(\texttt{ass:auxiliary-iid}\), and \(\texttt{ass:sample-independence}\), and their capacities are at least \(n/4\) and \(N/2\).  Draw independent Poisson prefix lengths with one fourth of these capacities as means.  On overflow output zero; otherwise use the all-heavy inverse-count statistic in \(\texttt{lem:poisson-hybrid-risk}\) and clip it to \([-1,1]\).  The ideal Poisson risk is bounded, by (11)--(12) in that lemma, by
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{N^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
Clipping cannot increase squared error because \(\tau(P)\in[-1,1]\).  If a Poisson variable has mean one fourth of its available capacity, the exponential-moment bound gives overflow probability at most \(e^{-c n}+e^{-cN}\le C/n\).  Coupling the ideal and overflow statistics therefore adds at most \(4C/n\) to risk.

The preceding statistic uses auxiliary randomization only through two integer prefix lengths.  Its conditional expectation given \((\mathcal L_n,\mathcal U_m)\) is a finite sum over all nonoverflow prefix pairs.  Jensen's inequality for squared loss makes its risk no larger, so this conditional expectation is the asserted deterministic total computable estimator in \(\mathcal T_{n,m,d}\).  For \(n<12\), use zero; since \(\tau(P)^2\le1\le12/n\), enlarging \(C_\epsilon\) covers these finitely many cases.  Taking the supremum and then the infimum in \(\texttt{def:minimax-risk}\) proves the final assertion.
